clue.text: Perhaps one shut a gap?

indicators.note: 'perhaps' says the following words are only one possible arrangement of the letters, so they may be rearranged

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about whether a single closing might seal up an opening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps one shut' reads like a guess at mending the gap, but 'one' is just the numeral I to be mixed with SHUT and A.
explanation.definitionFit: A hiatus is a pause or break in continuity, a synonym for a gap.

clue.text: The acre is roughly 40% of it

definitions.text: The acre is roughly 40% of it

indicators.note: 'roughly' means not exactly, so the preceding words are given only in rough order

parts.note: the two words as written, all seven letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A factual statement comparing two units of land area.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the definition and the wordplay: 'roughly' also does honest work in the fact, since an acre is about 0.405 of the metric unit.
explanation.definitionFit: A hectare is ten thousand square metres, about two and a half acres, so an acre is roughly forty per cent of one.

clue.text: It's injurious to cut off headdress

indicators.note: cutting off a word's head removes its first letter

parts.note: malign means harmful or injurious
a split word giving no letters: its first half closes the deletion signal and its second half is the definition

explanation.surface: A warning that a headdress can do harm and should be removed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'headdress' looks like one word but splits into 'head' (part of the deletion signal) and 'dress', the definition. To dress ranks is the military term for lining soldiers up.
explanation.definitionFit: In drill, to dress a line of troops is to straighten it, putting everyone into proper alignment.

clue.text: Take a turn with silent cooking in the kitchen

definitions.note: describes the answer by where it is found rather than naming it

parts.note: a U-turn, the letter shaped like a turn back

indicators.note: cooking transforms ingredients, so the word before it is mixed up

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice to take your turn at quiet cooking in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take a turn' reads like taking turns at the stove; the turn is the U of a U-turn.
explanation.definitionFit: A utensil is a tool or implement used in the kitchen, such as a spoon or whisk.

clue.text: Patrol leader like mother — it's in the blood

parts.note: PL is the Scouting abbreviation for a patrol leader
as means like, in comparisons
an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A Scout leader who takes after their mother, a trait running in the family.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Scouts a patrol leader is abbreviated PL. 'It's in the blood' sounds like inherited character, but is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: Plasma is the pale liquid component of blood in which the cells are suspended.

clue.text: Old reformer found everything held up by his superior

indicators.note: something held is gripped inside something else

parts.note: a lord is a feudal superior

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading the word from bottom to top

parts.note: all means everything

explanation.surface: A historical reformer discovers his master is supporting his whole cause.
explanation.walkthrough: Lollards were followers of John Wycliffe in 14th-century England, early church reformers.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lollards were medieval English religious dissenters who sought reform of the Church before the Reformation.

clue.text: One for the road — a quick gin, perhaps?

parts.note: speed is quickness, here as the first part of a compound
a gin is a kind of snare or trap

explanation.surface: A last drink before leaving: a fast gin, the classic 'one for the road'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One for the road' is the idiom for a final drink, and 'gin' seems to confirm it, but here gin is a trap and the road is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: A speed trap is something set up on a road by police to catch drivers going too fast.

clue.text: The skilled worker in Cathcart is a necessary part of the Cape economy

indicators.note: 'in' says the answer sits inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: the letters run across the end of Cathcart, through 'is a' and into the start of necessary
surface padding that completes the picture and gives no letters

explanation.surface: A craftsman in the South African town of Cathcart is vital to the Eastern Cape's economy.
explanation.walkthrough: Cathcart is a small town in South Africa's Eastern Cape; the rest of the clue just completes the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: An artisan is a craftsperson, a worker trained in a manual trade.

clue.text: He painted a vessel with a little boat on board

indicators.note: on board means inside a ship, written as the steamship letters around the rest

parts.note: a ship, abbreviated SS for steamship; being on board puts the rest inside it
a tub is a vessel, both container and slang for a boat

indicators.note: a little of a word is just its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of boat

explanation.surface: An artist painted a ship carrying a small boat.
explanation.walkthrough: George Stubbs was the 18th-century English painter famous for his horses. 'On board' is the convention for putting letters inside SS.
explanation.definitionFit: George Stubbs was an English artist, best known for his paintings of horses such as Whistlejacket.

clue.text: Premature demise may be hated

parts.note: surface reading: an early death is something people would loathe
setter's reading: the second word of the answer, rearranged by accident, can become hated

explanation.surface: A grim observation that dying too soon is something to be loathed.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse anagram: read the answer as an instruction, 'accidental' as the mixing signal applied to the five-letter second word, and the result is 'hated'.
explanation.definitionFit: A coroner's verdict for a death caused by mishap rather than illness or intent, which typically cuts life short.

clue.text: Where reels of film may be seen — or heard

definitions.text: Where reels of film may be seen

indicators.note: 'or heard' asks for the place name as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: film reels are stored in round metal cans

explanation.surface: A description of a place where films are shown and listened to.
explanation.walkthrough: Cannes, on the French Riviera, hosts the famous film festival; said aloud by English speakers it sounds like the cans film is kept in.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cannes Film Festival screens new movies every May, so it is a place where film reels are watched.

clue.text: Flatter and not so piquant

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to coax with flattery, a verb
second meaning: read as two parts, somewhat bland, more mild

explanation.surface: A comparison: something both flatter and less spicy, like a dull dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flatter' looks like the comparative of flat, matching 'not so piquant'; it is in fact the verb to flatter. The second meaning splits the answer as bland plus -ish.
explanation.definitionFit: To blandish is to coax with flattery; split jokingly, bland-ish means rather mild in flavour.

clue.text: He's admitted cruel manipulation in the course of his labours…

definitions.text: in the course of his labours
definitions.note: describes the hero by his famous labours rather than naming him

indicators.note: to be admitted is to be let inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe

indicators.note: manipulating something works it into a new shape, so the word before is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A man confesses to cruel scheming while carrying out his work.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this clue to the next; the Greek hero was set twelve labours as penance.
explanation.definitionFit: Hercules is the mythical Greek strongman famed for performing twelve near-impossible tasks known as his labours.

clue.text: Feast of cold and cooked meals

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

indicators.note: cooked food is transformed, so the word after it is mixed up

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A banquet made up of cold dishes and hot cooked ones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cold and cooked meals' reads as a menu; 'and' is kept as letters, not a joiner.
explanation.definitionFit: Candlemas is the Christian festival on 2 February marking the Presentation of Christ, a church feast day.

clue.text: …being brave and beloved, but heartless

indicators.note: without a heart means the central letter is taken out

parts.note: darling means a beloved person

explanation.surface: Continuing the hero's story: courageous and loved, yet without feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: Daring describes someone bold and willing to take risks, which is close to courageous.

clue.text: Vegetable pot found in the dump

indicators.note: something found in a place is located inside it

parts.note: a tip is a rubbish dump
an urn is a kind of pot

explanation.surface: A cooking pot of vegetables discovered thrown away at the rubbish dump.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a tip is a refuse dump.
explanation.definitionFit: The turnip is a round white root vegetable.

clue.text: Ignorant woman took the English to war

parts.note: Una is a woman's name
taken as written
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: An uninformed woman led the English into battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'took the English to war' sets the English letter after WAR.
explanation.definitionFit: To be unaware of something is to have no knowledge of it, much like being ignorant.

clue.text: Spoken prayer that's plain

indicators.note: something spoken is heard rather than read, so we go by its sound

parts.note: a prayer said with a short extra syllable on the end

explanation.surface: A prayer said aloud in simple, plain words.
explanation.walkthrough: The homophone is loose: prayer plus a trailing 'ee' sound. 'Plain' looks like an adjective for the prayer but is the noun for flat land.
explanation.definitionFit: A prairie is a vast flat grassland, as in North America, which is a kind of plain.

clue.text: Ovation for leading car overtaking

indicators.note: the leading part of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of car
lapping a rival is overtaking them a full circuit ahead

explanation.surface: Applause for the race leader as he overtakes another car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading car' looks like the front-runner in a race; it is simply the first letter of car.
explanation.definitionFit: An ovation is a round of applause, and clapping is the act of applauding.

clue.text: Walk by the river

parts.note: surface reading: a stroll along a riverbank
setter's reading: the answer is the name before 'Walk' in a famous London street beside the Thames

explanation.walkthrough: Cheyne Walk is a historic street in Chelsea, London, running along the Thames embankment; 'Walk' is part of its name, not a stroll.
explanation.definitionFit: The Chelsea street named Cheyne Walk lies along the north bank of the Thames, home to many famous residents.

clue.text: This could set many free

indicators.note: set free, the letters are released from their order and can rearrange

parts.note: the two words as written, seven letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A remark that this measure could release a great many prisoners.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: the letters of 'set many', freed, spell the answer, which is what frees prisoners.
explanation.definitionFit: An amnesty is an official pardon, often releasing large numbers of political prisoners at once.

clue.text: Girl gives boy a tall story

parts.note: Nat is a boy's name, short for Nathan or Nathaniel
taken as written
a tall story is an untruth

explanation.surface: A girl passes a boy an unlikely tale.
explanation.definitionFit: Natalie is a girl's given name, so it is an example of a girl.

clue.text: It may have a bearing on rushful possession

parts.note: in football or rugby, having possession means having the ball
a race is a rush, a dash at full speed

explanation.surface: Something with an influence on a hasty takeover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Have a bearing on' is the idiom for influencing, but the bearing here is a mechanical one: a ball race is the ring that holds ball bearings.
explanation.definitionFit: A ball race is the grooved ring in which the balls of a ball bearing run, so it houses bearings.

clue.text: Neat shot, though not centred with precision

indicators.note: without its centre, the middle letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: nice can mean neat or precise
to have a shot at something is to have a try

explanation.surface: A tidy shot in a game, though slightly off target, still showed accuracy.
explanation.definitionFit: A nicety is a fine detail or exactness, a matter of subtle precision.

clue.text: Officers take a drink

parts.note: two commanding officers, each abbreviated CO
taken as written

explanation.surface: Military officers having a drink together.
explanation.walkthrough: CO is the standard abbreviation for Commanding Officer; the plural gives two of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Cocoa is a hot chocolate beverage made from powdered cacao beans.

clue.text: Obsolete political tools?

parts.note: surface reading: outdated instruments of politics, such as discredited policies
setter's reading: two literal hand tools forming the emblem of a political system now largely defunct

explanation.walkthrough: The Soviet emblem was a crossed pair of workers' tools; with the USSR gone, the symbol is outdated.
explanation.definitionFit: The crossed implements of a worker and a peasant formed the communist emblem, a political symbol made of literal tools.

clue.text: The feast is almost oriental

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: eastern means oriental

explanation.surface: A claim that the festival is nearly an eastern one.
explanation.definitionFit: Easter is the Christian festival celebrating the Resurrection, one of the main feasts of the church year.

clue.text: Repeat action of a revolver

parts.note: surface reading: a pistol firing shot after shot
setter's reading: anything that revolves, going round and round again

explanation.walkthrough: A revolver suggests a gun and 'repeat action' its repeated firing, but a revolver is anything that spins.
explanation.definitionFit: To gyrate is to spin or whirl in circles, the repeated movement of something turning round.
